description: The nodes of the four-level tree on the left have no value labels. The node count doubles at each level: 1 root at level 1, 2 nodes at level 2, 4 at level 3, and 8 leaves at level 4. A gray note beneath the tree reads “Every level is full.”

Every non-leaf node has both a left and a right child. All 8 leaves line up on the fourth level, at the bottom of the tree. The heading on the right reads “Perfect binary tree.” A note in parentheses below it gives the alternative Chinese name in pinyin, mǎn èrchāshù.

frames.explanation: The figure has four levels and 15 nodes, and its height in edges is 3. In general, a perfect binary tree of height h has 2 to the power of (h+1) minus 1 nodes.
frames.title: Perfect binary tree: every level is full

summary: In a perfect binary tree, every level is full and all leaves are on the bottom level.
